oneLiner: 没有谁只用半边脑；分工是粗略的，整体协作才是常态。
oneLinerEn: No one uses just one hemisphere; division of labour is rough, and whole-brain cooperation is the default.
detail: 真相：左右脑确有粗略分工（如语言偏左），但任何复杂任务都两半球协同。所谓「左脑逻辑/右脑创意」是营销式简化。来源：脑成像研究一致显示任务激活横跨两半球。
detailEn: Truth: hemispheres do differ roughly (e.g. language leans left), but any complex task uses both. 'Left=logic, right=creative' is a marketing simplification. Source: imaging shows whole-brain activation.

oneLiner: 血型与性格无关，这是流行文化而非科学。
oneLinerEn: Blood type and personality are unrelated—pop culture, not science.
detail: 真相：大量研究未发现血型与人格特质有稳定相关；该说法主要流行于日本、韩国职场与婚恋。别用它给人贴标签。
detailEn: Truth: large studies find no stable link between blood type and traits; the belief is popular in Japan/Korea dating and hiring. Don't label people by it.

sources.label: 综述：血型-性格无相关
sources.labelEn: Review: no link between blood type and personality

term: 「多元智能测试能测出你擅长什么」
oneLiner: 加德纳的「多元智能」是框架，不是可精测的能力量表。
oneLinerEn: Gardner's 'multiple intelligences' is a framework, not a precise test.
detail: 真相：多元智能理论丰富了「智能不止 IQ」的视角，但市面「测试」多无信效度依据，不能据此定职业或分班。看趋势可以参考，下结论要谨慎。
detailEn: Truth: the theory broadened 'intelligence beyond IQ', but commercial 'tests' often lack validity and shouldn't sort careers or classes. Use as a lens, not a verdict.

termEn: We Only Use 10% of Our Brain
oneLiner: 全脑几乎时刻都在耗氧工作，10% 纯属都市传说。
oneLinerEn: The whole brain burns oxygen nearly all the time; 10% is a myth.
detail: 真相：脑成像显示即便静息，全脑也有广泛活动；任一部分受损都会带来功能缺损。来源：神经科学共识。
detailEn: Truth: imaging shows widespread activity even at rest; damage to any region causes deficits. Source: neuroscience consensus.

oneLiner: 记忆每次回想都被重写，会掺入后来信息。
oneLinerEn: Each recall rewrites memory, mixing in later information.
detail: 真相：记忆是可重构的，提问方式、他人说法都会改变回忆（错误记忆）。来源：洛夫特斯关于「误导信息效应」的研究。
detailEn: Truth: memory is reconstructive; wording and others' suggestions reshape it (false memories). Source: Loftus on the misinformation effect.

term: 「男女用脑方式完全不同，要分开教」
oneLiner: 两性大脑差异远小于个体间差异，分性别教学缺乏依据。
oneLinerEn: Sex differences in brain are far smaller than person-to-person ones; segregated teaching lacks basis.
detail: 真相：所谓「男女脑」多是群体平均的微小差异，落到个人几乎无效；按性别分班教学未被证明更优。来源：性别与认知的元分析综述。
detailEn: Truth: 'male/female brain' mostly reflects tiny group averages, useless per person; sex-segregated teaching isn't proven better. Source: meta-analyses on sex and cognition.

term: 「按学习风格（视觉/听觉型）教才有效」
oneLiner: 人确有偏好，但把教学匹配到「风格」并不提升成绩。
oneLinerEn: People have preferences, but matching teaching to 'styles' does not raise performance.
detail: 真相：大量研究未发现「风格匹配教学」的收益（学习风格假说缺乏证据）。内容本身更适合某种呈现方式（地理靠图、音乐靠听），而非因人而异。来源：Pashler 等 (2008) 综述。启示：与其贴标签，不如用好提取练习与多样化呈现。
detailEn: Truth: many studies find no benefit to matching instruction to 'styles'; the learning-styles hypothesis lacks evidence. Content suits a mode on its own terms (maps for geography, sound for music), not per person. Source: Pashler et al. (2008). Instead of labeling, use retrieval practice and varied presentation.

oneLiner: 打沙袋、大声叫嚷多在「排练」愤怒，反而强化而非消退。
oneLinerEn: Hitting a bag or shouting often rehearses anger, strengthening rather than draining it.
detail: 真相：宣泄假说认为释放能排空怒气，但实验发现强烈宣泄常升高后续攻击。发泄把“怒气”与“攻击行为”反复联结，反而练习了它们。真正有效的是冷静、认知重评与问题解决。来源：Bushman (2002) 等。
detailEn: Truth: catharsis theory says release empties anger, but experiments show vigorous venting often raises later aggression. Venting repeatedly pairs anger with attack—practicing it. Calming down, reappraisal and problem-solving work better. Source: Bushman (2002).

term: 「催眠能准确恢复被遗忘的记忆」
oneLiner: 催眠提升的不是准确度，而是自信——还会植入虚假记忆。
oneLinerEn: Hypnosis boosts confidence, not accuracy—and can plant false memories.
detail: 真相：被试在催眠下更易把暗示当作“想起”，事后却更坚信不疑，即“记忆膨胀”。催眠不能像录像回放，反易造出虚构细节。因此多法庭不采信催眠证词。来源：Lynn 等关于催眠与记忆的综述。
detailEn: Truth: under hypnosis people more often treat suggestions as 'remembering' yet feel more certain—memory inflation. Hypnosis cannot replay like a recording and readily fabricates detail, so many courts reject hypnotically refreshed testimony. Source: Lynn et al. on hypnosis and memory.

termEn: IQ Is Fixed and Effort Is Pointless
oneLiner: 智力有遗传成分但可受教育与环境影响，努力能提升表现。
oneLinerEn: Intelligence is heritable yet shaped by education and environment; effort lifts performance.
detail: 真相：遗传率不为 1，且随环境变化；弗林效应显示分数世代上升。“固定型思维”使人遇挫即弃，而“成长型思维”配合有效方法能持续进步。天赋影响起点，方法与环境影响能走多远。来源：Dweck (2006)。
detailEn: Truth: heritability is not 1 and varies with environment; the Flynn effect shows scores rising across generations. A 'fixed mindset' makes people quit at setbacks, while a 'growth mindset' with good methods sustains gains. Talent sets the starting point; method and environment set the distance. Source: Dweck (2006).

term: 「高自尊必然带来好表现与好人品」
oneLiner: 自尊与表现相关而非因果，盲目抬高还可能转成自负。
oneLinerEn: Self-esteem correlates with performance but rarely causes it; inflating it can breed narcissism.
detail: 真相：Baumeister 等综述发现，提升自尊的干预并不直接改善学业或行为；真正预测表现的是能力与具体反馈。空洞表扬可能养出脆弱的高自尊甚至攻击性。更可取的是建立在真实掌握上的“安全高自尊”。来源：Baumeister et al. (2003)。
detailEn: Truth: Baumeister's review found that boosting self-esteem does not directly improve schoolwork or conduct; skill and specific feedback predict performance. Empty praise can foster fragile, even aggressive, high self-esteem. Better is secure self-esteem built on real mastery. Source: Baumeister et al. (2003).

oneLiner: 内向关乎「精力从哪来」，害羞关乎「害怕评判」——两者可以各走各的。
oneLinerEn: Introversion is where energy comes from; shyness is fear of judgment—the two can run on separate tracks.
detail: 真相：内向（extraversion 的反面，荣格—艾森克意义上的一个维度）指人从独处与低刺激中恢复、在过多社交后耗竭；而害羞是对他人评价的焦虑，外向者同样可能害羞。二者统计相关却不同概念：一位爱演讲的外向者可能私下社恐，一位内向者也能在关心的议题上侃侃而谈。把内向误当缺陷，会催出「必须变外向」的规训；其实内向的优势在于深思、倾听与专注。来源：《安静》Susan Cain；人格特质研究。
detailEn: Truth: introversion (the low pole of extraversion, in the Jung–Eysenck sense) means recharging in solitude and low stimulation and draining after much socializing; shyness is anxiety about evaluation, and extroverts can be shy too. The two correlate yet are distinct concepts: a gregarious speaker may panic offstage, while an introvert can hold forth on a cause they care about. Mistaking introversion for a defect breeds 'must-be-outgoing' discipline; in fact its strengths are depth, listening and focus. Source: Cain, Quiet; trait research.

termEn: Eyewitness Memory Is Like a Video
oneLiner: 记忆每次被回忆就重拼一次，暗示、误导与情绪都能改写它——错的目击是冤案的首要来源。
oneLinerEn: Every recall reassembles memory; suggestion, misinformation and emotion can rewrite it—mis-ID is the top source of wrongful convictions.
detail: 真相：记忆不是回放，而是重构。洛夫特斯的实验显示，只把「撞碎（smashed）」换成「碰撞（hit）」，受试事后的速度估计就显著抬高，甚至更愿「记得」看到并不存在的碎玻璃；事后提问、 lineup 程序与同伴意见都会污染证词。情绪强烈也不会让记忆更准——闪光灯记忆主观鲜活，客观未必可靠。冤案平反统计中，误认是错误定罪的最大单一因素。改进靠双盲主持 lineup、先记录置信度、限制暗示性提问。来源： Loftus & Palmer (1974)。
detailEn: Truth: memory is reconstruction, not playback. Loftus showed that merely swapping 'smashed' for 'hit' in a question raised people's later speed estimates and even their false 'memory' of nonexistent broken glass; post-event questions, lineup procedure and peers all contaminate testimony. Strong emotion doesn't sharpen it—flashbulb memories feel vivid yet can miss. Misidentification is the single largest contributor to overturned wrongful convictions. Fixes: double-blind lineups, confidence recorded upfront, and limiting suggestive questioning. Source: Loftus & Palmer (1974).

termEn: Photographic Memory Can Be Trained in Anyone
oneLiner: 所谓过目不忘的图像记忆几乎只见于个别儿童，且无法靠训练普及到人人都会。
oneLinerEn: True eidetic image memory is seen, if at all, only in a few children—and cannot be trained into everyone.
detail: 市面上「全脑 / 波动速读」「记忆大师」课程宣称人人可练出过目成诵。真相是：发展心理学确记录过个别儿童在观看数秒后仍能看到残留图像，但此能力随年龄几乎消失，成人「照相记忆」从无可靠证据；竞赛级的记忆靠的是位置桩、数字编码等记忆术与刻意练习，而非某种图像直觉的天赋。把「练出的技巧」包装成「唤醒沉睡的天赋」，正是它的营销话术。
detailEn: 'Whole-brain / speed-reading' and 'memory master' courses claim anyone can learn to recall a page at a glance. In fact, developmental psychology has recorded a few children who still see a lingering image seconds after viewing, but it mostly fades with age, and adult 'photographic memory' has no solid evidence. Competition-level recall rests on mnemonics—the method of loci, number coding—built by deliberate practice, not a photographic gift. Repackaging 'a trained skill' as 'awakening a dormant talent' is exactly the sales pitch.

term: 「抑郁只是想太多、想开点就好」
termEn: Depression Is Just Overthinking—Snap Out of It
oneLiner: 抑郁是涉及情绪、躯体与认知的疾病，不是性格软弱，也难靠「振作」自愈。
oneLinerEn: Depression is a condition of mood, body and cognition—not a character flaw, and not something one simply snaps out of.
detail: 「你就是太闲 / 太玻璃心」是最常见也最伤人的劝说。事实上，抑郁伴随睡眠、食欲、精力与注意的改变，有神经与遗传的基础：轻症可靠心理治疗，中重度往往需要专业干预。「想开点」对一个已失去兴趣驱动的系统几乎无从下手，反而叠加自责与病耻感。恰当的援助是陪伴、去污名、鼓励就医，而不是一句「振作起来」。
detailEn: 'You're just idle / too sensitive' is the most common and most wounding advice. In truth depression alters sleep, appetite, energy and attention and has neural and genetic roots: mild cases may respond to psychotherapy, moderate-to-severe often need professional care. 'Cheer up' has nothing to grip in a system that has lost its drive, and only piles on self-blame and stigma. Right support means company, de-stigmatizing and encouraging treatment—not a 'pull yourself together'.

term: 「左撇子更聪明、更有艺术天赋」
termEn: Left-Handers Are More Creative or Gifted
oneLiner: 利手与创造力、智商之间并无稳定关系，「右脑等于艺术」只是连带编出的故事。
oneLinerEn: Handedness shows no reliable link to creativity or IQ; 'right brain equals artsy' is just a story bolted on.
detail: 人们爱说左撇子靠右脑、更直觉、更有天赋。但大规模研究里，左利手与右利手在智力、创造力上的均值差异微乎其微；某些领域（如部分持拍、对抗性球类）左利手比例偏高，多源于「对手不习惯其角度」的战术优势，而非天赋更高。利手受基因与环境共同影响，本身也不像「右脑理论」那样对称。把统计上的微小偏差说成「一族人的超能力」，是把相关当成了因果。
detailEn: The tale runs: left-handers lean on the right brain, so are more intuitive and gifted. But in large samples the average differences in intelligence and creativity between the hands are negligible; where left-handers are overrepresented (some racquet and contact sports) it mostly reflects the tactical edge of an unfamiliar angle, not a superior gift. Handedness is shaped by genes and environment and is no neat mirror of the right-brain story. Turning a tiny statistical tilt into 'a whole tribe's superpower' mistakes correlation for cause.

sources.label: Meta-analyses of handedness and cognitive ability

term: 「过了关键期就再也学不好外语」
termEn: Miss the Critical Period and You Can't Learn a Language
oneLiner: 敏感期确会影响口音，但把它说成「错过即终身锁死」，是对成年学习的低估。
oneLinerEn: A sensitive period does shape accent, but recasting it as 'miss it and you're locked out for life' underestimates adult learning.
detail: 「关键期假说」由伦内伯格提出，指语言习得存在生物时间窗，后被简化为「十几岁后学语言注定蹩脚」。证据其实更细：在接近母语的口音上，早期沉浸确有优势且随年龄下降；但在词汇、语法、读写等大量维度上，成年学习者照样高效，甚至借助母语的元语言意识后来居上。更准确的说法是「敏感期，外加动机、输入与方法」，而非一扇关了就再也不开的门。
detailEn: Lenneberg's critical-period hypothesis proposed a biological window for language, later flattened into 'learn after your teens and you're doomed to a bad accent'. The evidence is subtler: for near-native pronunciation early immersion does help and declines with age, yet across vocabulary, grammar and literacy adult learners thrive, even overtaking through metalinguistic insight from their first language. A truer frame is 'a sensitive period plus motivation, input and method'—not a door that shuts forever.
